$comment: Every Hawkes product Studio builds, playtests and reports on. Paths are relative to C:\Projects. local.serve: how Studio starts the product locally for playtests (npm: the dev server; static: python's http.server over a folder). playtests: what runs each day (where: local or live). quality: the quality bar, what "done" means for the product; reviews judge against it, and a scenario that meets it gets regression-only daily reviews until its build changes meaningfully (src/review.ts). Scenarios come from each game's playtest contract (docs/playtest.md). dev: developing on beta (src/dev.ts): front = the /dev/ front door port Caddy routes https://<sub>.hawkesgen.com/dev/* to, port = the dev server port in the beta working copy (web products), path = the devtools page.

products.name: Dose Of Destruction
products.about: A browser platform fighter (Babylon.js) with every main Hawkes IP character. The campaign is a TV show, from Open Mic (a walk-on with one skateboard, Exit Punk) to Encore. Fighters, poses and animations are AI-generated.
products.quality: From the menu a fight starts and ends; every fighter can be picked, moves, attacks and gets KO'd with readable hit feedback; campaign chapters play in order with their story beats; no crash or soft-lock. AI-generated art with uneven style between fighters is accepted.

products.name: PH Origins
products.about: A third-person story game (Babylon.js): one night in Hawkes Tower. The board meets, B3 writes back, Pierce Hawkes goes down to the vat and transforms. Levels 1-6 are playable; dialogue, voice lines and cutscenes.
products.quality: Levels 1-6 play start to finish with their cutscenes, dialogue and voice lines; the player always knows where to go and never gets stuck; the tone stays a corporate thriller turning to horror (per Lore.txt). Art fidelity beyond what the levels have now is not asked for.

products.name: Sick Of It
products.about: A 2D arcade bullet-dodger (Unity WebGL) with rewind: a sarcastic nobody chases the Overlord up 1,000 floors of Hell. Hell is repetition, so rewind is the hero's power. Slimes are villagers, never enemies. No office or work jokes.
products.quality: Menus work; a run climbs floors with dodging and rewind working; death sends you back down (the roguelite loop); the HUD and floor count are readable; tone per the story bible (deadpan hero, slimes are villagers, no office jokes).

products.name: Yooba Land
products.about: A 3D game (Unity URP, WebGL) about where Yooba came from: eat, grow, and find the way home.
products.quality: The game loads into the world; Yooba moves, eats and grows; the way home can be found; no crash, no falling through the world, no stuck camera. Prototype art and sparse content are accepted.

products.name: The Place Department
products.about: A prototype roguelike wave-defense game (Unity WebGL): Warrok, a bow-wielding brute, defends a pirate pianist from waves of birds. "Where things that should not exist are given an address."
products.quality: Prototype. A run starts; waves of birds come; Warrok can aim and shoot; the pianist can be defended or lost; a run ends with a result and can restart. Prototype art and placeholder UI are accepted.

products.name: I Can Be
products.about: A real-time simulation (Babylon.js) of a day in a developer's life; the character is "AI". Direction undecided.
products.quality: Direction undecided, so the bar is only that it runs: it loads and the day simulation runs without errors or a blank screen. Don't judge or suggest a direction.

products.name: Imagine Live TV
products.about: A choose-your-path video story, The Final Spark: you wake in a sewer, found by a rat; each choice is a page with a video. Plus a blog.
products.quality: Every branch page of The Final Spark loads its video and its choices go to the right next page (per the decision tree); the blog pages load; works on a phone.

products.name: Hawkes Biomedical
products.about: The corporate front of Hawkes Biomedical, a fictional pharma megacorp. It lists the product line as medical products, never games; the footer says it's fiction. Never mention B3, the vat or the creature. "We do not pitch a cure. We own the category."
products.quality: Every page loads with no broken links or images; it reads as a pharma company (products never called games, the footer says it's fiction, nothing about B3, the vat or the creature); works on a phone.

infra.name: Hawkes Studio
infra.about: J's cockpit (studio.hawkesgen.com): the daily build/playtest/review loop, backlog, reports, agent changes, beta lane and go live, Talk. Node 24 + TypeScript (type stripping), a plain-JS dashboard.

infra.name: Hawkes Gen
infra.about: The shared generative-AI service (gen.hawkesgen.com): the job queue, the AWS GPU fleet (ComfyUI), ElevenLabs, Claude, local tools, the library, usage and API keys, the build server and the playtester. Node 24 + TypeScript (type stripping), a plain-JS dashboard.

$comment_infra: Hawkes Studio and Hawkes Gen as agent targets (src/agents.ts): a change is a pull request into main (no beta lane), verified by CI on the pull request, the checks and a smoke check of the changed service on a spare port. Approving merges into main, and the server deploys it itself. Not in "repos": the server's checkouts of these two only move through deploy/hawkes-pull.mjs.
$comment_repos: GitHub repo for each top-level folder (the server clones them into the same layout as C:\Projects).
$comment_previews: Beta sites: https://<subdomain>.hawkesgen.com/ is the product built from its beta branch (what going live ships), /c/<change id>/ an agent change (src/previews.ts; DNS and Caddy in deploy/deploy.mjs). Same login as Studio.
